To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dynamo bifucation in the Earth’s core is hysteretic.

(i) the dipolar and multipole dynamos are in a bistable regime for weak initial fields; (ii) the bistable regime is extended when approaching realistic parameters; (iii) the bistable region disappears when the initial field is too large.

(i) the dynamo bifucation is subcritical in the dipolar branch, and supercritical in the multipolar branch; and (ii) the dynamo is bistable in the multipolar region, i.e. both dipolar and multipole dynamos can coexist.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamo bifucation in a configuration applicable for the Earth’s liquid core and the results are of interest for the understanding of the Earth’s magnetic field and geomagnetic reversals.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dipole-dominated dynmos are the most efficient dynamos and that the multipolar ones are less efficient.
the Earth’s magnetic field is a dipolar one, as it was for most of the past 3.5 billion years, because of the dipolar stability of the dynamo.
, for the parameter range explored here, dipole-dominated dynamo are more likely than multipolar dynamos, and that the latter can be obtained only for very specific conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamo bifucation depends strongly on the flow structure which is itself controlled by the magnetic Prandt number.
, in order to obtain a dipole-dominated dynamo, the convective flow has to be weak, the magnetic field has to be weak and the Ekman number has to be small.
the dipolar field is the preferred solution for low Rayleigh and magnetic Reynolds number and the multipolar field for high Rayleigh number.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dipole field is not a robust feature of planetary dynamo simulations, and that it is not necessarily a stable state of the dynamo.
, when the initial magnetic field is weak, the dipolar and multipole branches of the bifurcation coexist in the parameter range explored.
the nature of the bifurcation is not only determined by the control parameters but also by the initial field.
